correctness.rationale: For three candidates, both rules expose exactly the alternatives obtained by omitting a weakest edge of a majority 3-cycle, with all tied weakest edges retained. For four candidates the frozen C verifier exhausts all labeled one-, three- and five-voter profiles; the independently coded frozen Python verifier exhausts all \(98280\) anonymous five-voter profiles using simple-path Schulze scores and Tideman-style ranking elimination for Ranked Pairs. A fresh independent anonymous replay in this audit reproduced the weighted histogram \(6858144,275760,591120,185760,51840\), strict containment on every divergence, and canonical margin types \((-3,-3,1,-1,-1,-1)\) with weight \(11520\) and \((-3,-1,1,1,-1,-1)\) with weight \(40320\).
correctness.risk: The statement depends on the set-valued parallel-universe convention; a fixed external tie-break is a different rule.

value.rationale: The first disagreement layer between two major Condorcet methods is a natural structural boundary. The result does more than count examples: it gives exact prevalence, the one-sided winner-set relation and a complete two-type weighted-majority geometry.
value.risk: No formula is claimed for larger electorates or five-plus candidates.

final_claim: With majority-margin strength and parallel-universe tie-breaking for Ranked Pairs, Schulze and Ranked Pairs have identical winner sets for every three-candidate profile and for all four-candidate one- and three-voter profiles. Five voters are the first odd four-candidate electorate with divergence: exactly \(51840\) of \(24^5\) labeled profiles diverge, always with a two-candidate Ranked-Pairs set strictly contained in a three-candidate Schulze set, and exactly two candidate-relabeling majority-margin types occur.
limitations: Complete strict ballots and majority-margin strength.
Exact four-candidate census only through the first divergent odd electorate.
